headline: Break sits off Santa Rosa, blown out; Tuesday is the calm day
body:
Safety first: a small craft advisory runs through late tonight for everything outside the islands, including the Santa Rosa waters and the outer banks — NW 20 to 30 kt, seas 8 to 11 ft out west and 7 to 10 ft outside. The channel itself is mild, 2 to 4 ft with light wind going SW 10 this afternoon, but the run is the problem, not the harbor. Tuesday the advisory drops: channel 2 to 3 ft, SE 10 to 15 early turning SW, the triangle middle 4.1 ft, patchy morning fog.

Tuesday is the day. The triangle holds no 64–68 water either day — corners read 72.9 west, 73.6 east, 70.8 at the south point today, and 73.9, 73.4, 71.6 tomorrow — so start the south point and work the southern edge into the basin, the only cool side available, and stay on bait. Today's only break water is Santa Rosa at 65.7, and it is unfishable; by Tuesday it warms to 70.3. Osborn at 71.4 and San Nicolas at 69.7 are not worth 68 or 73 nm.
